# mixed-keys fixture

Two complete backup sets in ONE object namespace, written by the Nyx Backup
app's real writer under two different master keys:

| set | master key | readable by |
|-----|-----------|-------------|
| `11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111` | `000102...1e1f` | the "our machine" key |
| `55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555` | `a0a1a2...bebf` | the "other machine" key |

Both keys are synthetic and public on purpose; the content is throwaway test
data.

## What it is for

Master keys are per machine, and one endpoint can hold sets from several
machines.  Google Drive makes that the normal case, not a corner case: the
`appDataFolder` is a single flat per-account space with no sub-folders, and the
Connect screen has no path field for Drive, so every machine backing up to that
Google account shares one namespace.

Recovery must therefore treat "present but unopenable with this key" as an
ordinary state and SAY SO.  Before the `undecryptable_sets` count existed, such
sets were skipped silently - a user hunting for a machine that was in fact
backed up saw a short list and concluded their data was gone.

`tests/mixed_key_discovery.rs` asserts:

- our key lists our set and reports the other as `undecryptable_sets: 1`
- the other key sees the mirror image (so the count follows the key, not
  set ordering)
- a key that opens NOTHING is a hard error with guidance, not an empty list

## Regenerating

From the main Nyx Backup repo, run the generator twice into this directory:

```bash
cargo run -p bkp-engine --example gen_recovery_fixture -- <this-dir>
cargo run -p bkp-engine --example gen_recovery_fixture -- <this-dir> --foreign
```

See `crates/bkp-restore/tests/fixtures/README.md` for why fixtures are
committed as bytes rather than generated by this repo.
